Elon Musk: Flight 14 is the last before they try to catch Starship

"We've got Flight 14 coming up of Starship, and this will be the last flight before we attempt to catch the ship. So if this flight goes well, then on Flight 15 we will try to catch the ship… once we can re-fly the ship, we will have made the first fully reusable orbital rocket."

• Flight 14 — last before catch attempt
• Flight 15 — try catch with the tower arms
• Re-fly ship + booster — first fully reusable orbital rocket
• Odds on first catch: at least 50–60%

Last flight already simulated a tower catch ~1,000 miles NW of Australia — would have caught it if a tower were there. One more flight to double-check so debris never rains on people.

Elon Musk on AI and the size of the economy.

"I think AI will probably increase the global economy by 20 to 30%."

"Meaning on the order of 20 to 30 trillion dollars per year."

That is digital AI alone — software, engineering, anything that does not require hands on atoms.

"AI will be able to do anything digital, anything that does not require shaping of atoms by hand."

"Probably by the end of next year."

• 20–30% — digital AI lift to global GDP
• ~$20–30T / year — order of magnitude
• End of next year — anything digital
• Atoms by hand — the bottleneck robots remove

Digital first.
Then robotics.
Then the economy stops looking like today’s.

Elon Musk wants peer review for AI: labs test each other’s models before release

"Instead of just kind of grading your own homework, you would at least have competitors grading yours, and raising the alarm if they see concerns… It's something that can be done immediately… peer review, where the leading AI companies all test each other's models before release."

Peer review = other labs check your model before you ship it.
Not you grading your own homework.
He says it can start now.

FSD 14.3.9 takes on DOWNTOWN San Jose.I had Grok pick every location, and FSD just handled a major downtown like it was nothing. 

Busy intersections, pedestrians stepping off curbs, buses pulling out, tight one-ways, last-second lane changes — it read the chaos and kept moving with this calm, confident flow that still doesn’t feel real.

The reactions are snappy. The pathing is decisive. 

It doesn’t freeze, doesn’t get weirdly timid, and it doesn’t drive like a robot guessing. It just… drives. Watching it thread a dense downtown after Grok built the whole route is wild.

Can’t believe how far this has come. FSD is actually insane now.
